productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very fun coloring book for AutumnVery fun coloring book for Autumn
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This would have been my dream coloring book when I was maybe 10 years old! I still love it, as a lot of the images are laid-out like something from a magazine or illustrated book--where there's text with images. This makes it easier for me to color, rather than me feeling overwhelmed at trying to approach some intricate masterpiece of line-art!! It's very approachable and fun to color.Unlike some of this artist's other coloring books, this one actually seems like a legit Samhain/ Halloween themed coloring book throughout. There are a few pages with big blank areas, but it's not like some of the others where it's all wheel of the year/ monthly planner stuff with the calendar markings removed.There's a lot of fun holiday info and suggestions. It makes me feel quite nostalgic, as it reminds me of books from childhood about Halloween (especially the ones about Halloween party ideas).The art is really cute and whimsical. I have read a lot of criticism that the artist churns out a lot of sloppy work and repeated elements.  This is too true--but I try to bear in mind that she's probably doing all this work under deadline for yearly planners, then it's being recycled into these coloring books.  You will find tons of the same elements like they have been copy-pasted across almost every page--especially the pumpkins! There's a loooooot of pumpkins and it seems like it's just the same 3 that are repeated 50 times (or more!) in this book. That gets annoying...but trying to look at the bright side of it...once I have figured out how to color that one pumpkin, or whatever image she's repeated, perfectly then it takes the pressure off of me the next time I encounter it. I already know how to handle that, so I can focus on figuring out how to best approach other things in the new image.  If you are looking for intricate, perfect, mystical masterpieces to color, then this isn't the book for you. This book is more about having fun and getting into the Samhain/ Halloween spirit while coloring.The author does have several helpful videos posted online where she records herself coloring some of her pages.  She gives advice and teaches skills--and only uses a common brand of pencil that you probably already own!This coloring book is fairly thick, and has way more pages than most adult coloring books, so I guess the relatively high price for something printed on copier paper is kind-of justified.  I have been very gentle with the book, and only colored a few pages, but the binding is already falling apart!! You can perhaps see that in my final photo...one which I included for a different reason altogether.My last photo is to show the crazy warning label that is inside this coloring book!! Ok, to be honest, when I first got the book, I was a little bit put-off by the whole thing (and I mean before I found the warning label). Had I flipped through the book at a store, there's no way I would have bought it because it's totally a little kids coloring book from start to finish...a kids book with full-on nudity. I assumed I had accidentally purchased something designed for children from neo-pagan/ wiccan homes. Have anyone who is unfamiliar with it flip through the book and ask them who the target audience would be. I betcha they will say that it's a coloring book for gradeschool through middle school age children.  I remember being a very young child and arguing with my parents about something they found offensive on TV; I don't remember what it was, I just remember it was a cartoon and I said "that's for me because it is a cartoon!" When something looks like it is clearly for children, kids are trained to know that it "is for them" like I said back when I was approx 5 years old. This book looks like it is designed for kids, but there's a warning that it isn't--a very peculiarly worded warning: "This book is not for children. And so it shall be." They're assuming the reader is conditioned to hearing phrases such as "so mote it be" and variations of that to close prayers and spells. Step outside of your conditioning and read the actual words of that entire warning and what they actually say...not what you assume the author is trying to say. If I were Wiccan, I would be offended because other major religions have coloring books, but none of them ever have warning labels about their inherit risks and dangers. I think this warning label is paradoxically trying to make the book more appealing, especially to rebellious young people. Oh, and what about that cumbersome list of activities we "agree to do" (albeit at our own risk)? I don't "agree" to do anything...except pay the asking price to receive the book...and yeah I reckon I agree to be bound by international copy right laws lol.So, like I say, I wouldn't have bought this in a store because it's obviously for kids....and I especially wouldn't have purchased anything that feels the need to include a wacky warning label like that one!!  But I did buy it through the magic of the Internet where you never truly know what you're getting!! And I am glad to have it.  It's probably in my top 5 favorite coloring books out of the many that I own.

It was kinda comforting to me to get read the included rituals for working with Ancestors and I also loved seeing the "family tree" page that you can color and include drawings or photos of your family and Ancestors.Honestly, The Season of the Witch is definitely one of my very favourites by Amy. You can tell the amount of thought, time and love she put into this book. It includes everything like crafts, rituals, spells, altar ideas, adorable games to color and play, lots of correspondence pages (my favorite), different types of divination to try, yummy snacks and treats to make, postcards, a banner and way more! Even if you do not color, this is a great book to own for ideas and info to celebrate Samhain. And This would also make for a perfect Witchy gift idea. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Book APPROVED! By Samhain the Sphynx~Ok, ghouls & gals- Listen. It’s a total escape to a world that exists parallel to ours. You know the one I speak of. I can’t wait to start making this my own, as I have done to my Hedge & Alchemy books. I love to brew a cup of my favorite tea put on some Celtic music and zone out for a bit in one of Amy’s books. For me it’s a “get away” of sorts. A breath of fresh air. I’m able to decompress from the rush of everyday and renew my mind. Season of the witch stands out with its traditional Halloween colors and hard cover which is my favorite. I feel like I’m a student at Hogwarts holding this book (one can dream). The pages are of a nice thickness and there  are blank pages on the back of every printed so whatever medium you choose doesn’t bleed onto another drawing rendering it useless. Further, there are plenty of blank pages for your own thoughts, notes and spells. Amy thought of all the details in this book. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Witches, brooms and spells make this a fun coloring book for the Halloween season or anytime of year for those fascinated by witches and the occult. The coloring book features witches across the centuries from Harry Potter’s Professor Minerva McGonagall to Morgan Le Fey. The pictures range from fairly simple to more complex, so both adults and children can enjoy them. I also like leaving a blank page on the reverse of the picture.
